newsitem.title: UK: European shares chase Wall St bull.
newsitem.headline: European shares chase Wall St bull.

text.p: European shares posted solid gains on Thursday as Wall Street extended its overnight recovery after a week of losses, but there were growing signs of nervousness.

French shares, which also had a small rate cut to celebrate, led the way higher in Europe, with the CAC 40 index rising 38.05 points, or 1.54 percent, to close at a record of 2,503.06. London's FTSE 100 index ended up 20.9 points, or 0.5 percent, at 4,228.4, while Germany's DAX index closed up 18.12 points, or 0.6 percent, at 3,017.32.

In New York the Dow industrial average was up 20.78 points, or 0.31 percent, at 6,761.90. On Wednesday it closed 84.66 points higher at 6,740.74, its best gain since January 3 when it surged 102 points.
U.S. shares rose on the back of weekly jobless claims, which came in higher than forecast, lifting U.S. Treasuries.

Shares in London, Europe's largest bourse, ended higher after moving tentatively upwards in the wake of a rejuvenated Dow, but fears of another reversal on Wall Street capped the FTSE's gains and kept volume subdued.
"The Dow has been incredibly volatile," said Credit Lyonnais Laing strategist Savvas Savouri in London. "The intraday movement has been so violent recently there's no discernable trend to follow."

Dealers said the main focus of the day was Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress. His prepared comments failed to mention current economic conditions, but gave U.S. Treasuries a mild boost.
Analysts said market uncertainty was likely to persist ahead of interest rate meetings in Britain and the United States next week, when rates could rise to counter the threat of inflation.
Higher interest rates would sorely test the world's share markets, many of which are at or near record levels, by making returns on alternative investments and cash more attractive.

French stocks rallied to historic highs in heavy volume, propelling the blue-chip CAC-40 index above the 2,500 points barrier for the first time, after the Bank of France trimmed its leading intervention rate to 3.10 percent from 3.15. The timing of the move largely surprised financial markets.

The market was also lifted by a 15.53 percent surge in shares of electrical engineering group Alcatel Alsthom, which said it expected to show net income of 2.5 billion francs for 1996, higher than analysts had expected.

German shares also finished firmly ahead, with a strong showing by U.S. stocks and the dollar pushing the DAX index through the 3,000 point level and allowing the gains to be extended in late German trade.
Star performer on the DAX was Allianz after investment house Goldman Sachs raised its rating on the insurer.
The upgrade sparked a rally in Allianz that saw its shares rise some five percent to a record high at 3,088 marks before easing in post-bourse trade to 3,062.50.
In currencies, the dollar was in consolidation mode in late European trade, taking a breather from its recent volatility and given little inspiration by Greenspan's testimony.
The dollar edged back below 1.64 marks following the prepared testimony which disappointed some by not commenting on current economic conditions.
Greenspan said a stronger dollar tended to restrain import prices but exchange rates "almost never" determined the outcome of Federal Open Market Committee decisions on interest rates.

The dollar's slip late Wednesday and overnight was seen as shortlived by analysts and a necessary correction from this week's highs on the yen and mark ahead of key economic events next month, particularly the February 8 G7 meeting in Berlin.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6385 marks and 121.55 yen compared with late Wednesday's European levels of 1.6428 marks and 121.99 yen.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was up 20.9 points at 4,228.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 38.05 points at 2,503.06.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 18.12 points at 3,017.32. The Ibis DAX index of post-bourse trade stood at 3,018.58, up 20.63 at the close.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $347.35, sharply down from Wednesday's close of $351.05 after smashing through support at $350 on talk of central bank selling.
